content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1

Let's parse: It's a methoxy phenyl attached to amide linking to a triazine? Actually c2nnn(... )c2N is a 1,2,4-triazine? The core is a 1,2,4-triazine (c2nnn...c2N). The substituent is Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 (a phenyl with a side chain bearing a fluoromethylpiperidine? Actually CN4CC(F)C4 is a N-methyl-azetidine? Wait N4CC(F)C4 is a 3-member? Actually N4CC(F)C4 is a azetidine (four-membered ring) with fluorine on carbon. So side chain is phenyl-CH2- attached to that heterocycle.

Goal: propose retrosynthesis using commercially available building blocks.

We need leaves commercially available, total price <= $9999.

We have some building blocks found: methoxy aniline (COc1ccc(N)cc1) price $50.6 for 100g. Good.

We have the triazine core with amine and carboxylate? The building block "NC1=NN=CC(=N1)C(O)=O" is a 1,2,4-triazin-5-ylamine with carboxylic acid (maybe). Price $1216 per gram. That's okay.

But we need the triazine with N-substituted (C attached to phenyl). The target has a triazine with N attached to phenyl-CH2-... and also an exocyclic N (maybe NH). The building block could be the triazine core with NH2 and COOH; we could convert COOH to amide with aniline? Actually target has amide linking phenoxy aniline to carbonyl attached to triazine carbonyl? Wait target: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1. So the amide is between aniline (para-methoxy phenyl) and carbonyl attached to triazine carbon (C=O attached to triazine carbon). So we need to form amide between aniline and carboxylic acid of triazine? The triazine has a carbonyl attached to it (C=O) as part of amide. So we could start from triazine carboxylic acid (NC1=NN=CC(=N1)C(O)=O). Convert to acid chloride then amidate with aniline (methoxy aniline). That yields the amide.

Then we need to attach the phenyl-CH2-... substituent onto the triazine nitrogen (the N at position 2 maybe). The triazine core has an exocyclic N (the "N" after c2nnn(... )c2N). That is an amino group attached to the triazine ring (maybe at position 6). In the target, that N is attached to the phenyl-CH2-... group via a carbon (C attached to phenyl). Actually the SMILES: c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N. So the triazine ring has a substituent at one N (the N is part of ring) attached to Cc3... (a benzyl). And also an exocyclic N (c2N) attached to the ring (maybe at position 5). So the triazine has two substituents: a benzyl group and an NH (exocyclic). The building block we have (NC1=NN=CC(=N1)C(O)=O) has an exocyclic NH2 and a carboxylic acid. It lacks the benzyl substituent. So we need to introduce benzyl onto the triazine nitrogen via N-alkylation.

Thus retrosynthesis: Step 1: Start from triazine core with NH2 and COOH (commercial). Alkylate the exocyclic NH2 with benzyl bromide (or appropriate benzyl halide) to give N-benzyl triazine (still with COOH). Then amidate with methoxy aniline to give final product.

Alternatively, we could first amidate then N-alkylate; but N-alkylation after amide formation may be hindered. Better to N-alkylate first.

Thus we need benzyl bromide with phenyl-CH2- attached to phenyl bearing CN4CC(F)C4 side chain. That is a complex benzyl halide: Br-CH2-Ph-(CN4CC(F)C4). We need to see if that is commercially available. Search.
